name: Clarithromycin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 250 or 500 mg every 12 hours for 7 to 14 days

usual_adult_dose.indication: H. pylori (with amoxicillin and a PPI)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 500 mg every 8 or 12 hours for 10 to 14 days

key_interactions.action: Contraindicated in kidney or liver impairment; reduce colchicine dose otherwise.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: CYP3A-metabolized calcium channel blockers (amlodipine, nifedipine, diltiazem, verapamil)
key_interactions.effect: Hypotension and acute kidney injury, mainly in older adults (label).

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Tacrolimus, cyclosporine, other narrow-margin CYP3A substrates

serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
Drug-interaction toxicity (colchicine, statins, calcium channel blockers)

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to clarithromycin or any macrolide
Cisapride, pimozide, ergot alkaloids, lurasidone, lomitapide, lovastatin, simvastatin
Colchicine in kidney or liver impairment
Previous cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction with clarithromycin
monitoring: QT and electrolytes when at risk

pk.half_life: 3 to 4 hours (250 mg every 12 hours); 5 to 7 hours (500 mg)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 20% (250 mg) to 30% (500 mg) unchanged in urine
